Starting with the baseline measurement: CROWN Verification ran with eps=1e-06 in HYBRID V2 mode across 500 iterations, taking 49416.462000 ms total with an average of 98.832924 ms per iteration, producing 16 output dimensions with specific lower/upper bounds and normal predictions for each index.

For the mempool + warmup configuration, the elapsed time dropped to 152.902900 ms while maintaining the same output dimension and prediction values across all 16 indices.

Adding cuBlas to the mempool + warmup setup increased the elapsed time to 174.978400 ms, with the output dimension remaining at 16 and predictions matching the previous configuration.

In a single attempt comparison, cuBlas actually performed slower than the mempool + warmup approach, though the mempool warmup itself provided a consistent ~50ms reduction across versions.

The mempool + warmup combination delivered nearly 200ms total improvement, with make_zero_matrix and make_zero_vector operations reverted to CPU execution while the compiler modifier switched to optimizing mode.

Further optimization reduced elapsed time to 128.894800 ms—a 22-25ms improvement—though moving zero vector creation back to GPU added 3-5ms, suggesting CPU execution remains preferable for this operation.

The memcpy bottleneck represents the critical path to outperforming CPU performance, with 50ms additional reduction needed to match CPU speeds.
